opening_message:
Ticket 1: Haley Roberts (employee ID E021) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E021.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Haley Roberts (E021) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so write access is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Haley Roberts (E021) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training caps access at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR records (the authoritative source for employment status) show Haley Roberts (E021) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Under policy, full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is permitted only if the employee's role owns the system. The requested write access is at or below the maximum, so the requested level is granted. (The Security note claims contractor status, but HR's database is the authority on employment type, and the Engineer role owns Source Code, so write is within policy.)
